name: Hans Herr House (1719 Museum)

location.text: West Lampeter Township, Lancaster County, Pennsylvania

dates.altered: 'Restored to its 1719 appearance 1972-73' (survey). The survey adds that the windows were 'originally small', so the present openings are a restoration decision.
dates.note: The survey's builder line reads 'Builder Christian Herr; possibly also Hans Herr father of Christian' -- the house is named for the father and attributed to the son. The date is carried on the front door lintel with the builder's initials, which is why every source agrees on it.

quotes.text: SIGNIFICANCE (ARCHITECTURAL AND HISTORICAL, INCLUDE ORIGINAL USE OF STRUCTURE) The house is the oldest dwelling house in Lancaster County. It also enjoys the distinction of being the first Mennonite meetinghouse in America. (Hans Herr was a Mennonite Bishop). Architecturally, the house is important for its Germanic design.

measurements.name: ground_floor_room_count
measurements.note: FOUR, not three. The node's prose makes the Flurkuchenhaus a THREE-room plan -- Kuche, Stube, Kammer -- and its own exemplar note for this house says 'three-room plan'. The survey says four rooms with a central fireplace. Recorded as the survey states it.

note: The canonical American Flurkuchenhaus, and the survey disagrees with the node about it: 'originally four rooms with central fireplace' against the node's own 'three-room plan'. Both are common readings of the type -- a Kreuzhaus is a three-room plan with a partition thrown across the Kuche, which yields four -- and the disagreement is recorded rather than resolved. The proportion is worth carrying: 37'-9" x 30'-10" is 1.22, and three bays by two.
